dossier.summary: Kestrel Labs runs phishing simulations and short security training for dental and medical practices. Practices pay per seat per month.

strategy.intro: Small practices know they are a target but have no one whose job is security. Kestrel wins by making the practice manager look prepared before an insurer or auditor asks.
strategy.audience: Practice managers and office managers at dental groups and clinics with 3 to 30 locations. We skip hospitals; they buy through procurement and want a different product.
strategy.offer: A free phishing check: one simulated email to the front desk team, with the results sent to the manager the same week.
strategy.channels: Email first, since practice managers read their inbox between patients. LinkedIn is light here; we use it only for multi-location groups.
strategy.goal: Eight practices running the free check in two weeks.

data.sampling_criteria: Practice managers at US dental groups with three or more locations.
